# t1.1.1 — Re-verify additive users-table migration after Jackson startup remediation

## Result

Re-verified the existing additive Flyway migration after the backend corrected Jackson 3 configuration binding. No database or application source changes were needed. A clean Maven verification passed, including the full application-context/Jackson startup test and both users-migration integration tests.

Flyway logged that it applied version 2 (`create users table`) during startup, and the migration integration tests confirmed Hibernate-compatible persistence and a safe second Flyway invocation with the inserted user still readable.

## Verification Scope

- Reviewed the unchanged `V2__create_users_table.sql`, `User` entity, default H2/Flyway configuration, and migration integration tests.
- Confirmed the migration remains additive (`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`); there is no data rewrite, table drop, or destructive alteration.
- The migration integration tests still exclude Jackson autoconfiguration to isolate schema behavior. Separately, `ApplicationStartupIntegrationTest` now starts the full Spring context with Jackson enabled and verifies `Instant` serialization, so the former startup remediation is covered without weakening the application startup test.
- MySQL migration execution was not performed; the available verification uses the default H2 datasource in MySQL compatibility mode.
